title: Backend: annotate each portfolio position with its current signal
description: User request: every list of tickers in the UI must show its BUY/HOLD/SELL signal, including existing portfolio positions -- not just the watchlist (which api-watchlist already does). GET /api/portfolio's PositionOut currently enriches each position with market data (current_price/unrealized_pnl_pct) via an existing per-position pipeline in backend/app/api/routers/portfolio.py, but has no signal field. Extend PositionOut with nullable signal/confidence/confidence_band fields, computed by reusing the existing signal engine (backend/app/signals/engine.py's analyse()) against that same per-position market-data fetch -- do not implement a second/divergent signal computation. Follow the exact nullable-on-failure precedent already established by api-watchlist's WatchlistItemOut (a ticker whose signal can't be computed gets null fields, not a failed request or a dropped position) rather than inventing a new convention.

checklist.step: Add nullable signal/confidence/confidence_band fields to PositionOut in backend/app/api/schemas.py, with field descriptions per CLAUDE.md's API documentation standard.

Compute them in backend/app/api/routers/portfolio.py's get_portfolio, reusing the existing per-position market-data fetch and the signal engine's analyse() -- do not add a second signal computation path.

Follow api-watchlist's nullable-on-failure precedent exactly (a position whose signal can't be computed gets null fields, the endpoint still returns the position) -- record as a decisions entry only if any deviation from that precedent is needed, otherwise just cite it.
Tests: positions with a computable signal, a position whose signal computation fails (nullable fields), confirm current_price/unrealized_pnl_pct behavior is unaffected.
Run `python scripts/export_openapi.py` from backend/ and commit the updated backend/openapi.json.

decisions.decision: GET /api/portfolio's per-position signal computation reuses enrich_positions_with_price's already-fetched e.daily_ohlcv (no second daily fetch), but issues its own additional provider.get_weekly_ohlcv(ticker) call per position -- the same extra weekly fetch GET /api/portfolio/risk already makes for the same reason (Screen 1/Tide needs weekly history that enrich_positions_with_price never fetches). A position's signal fields go null if either that position's e.daily_ohlcv is None (its price fetch already failed) or the weekly fetch raises DataProviderError, mirroring api-watchlist's WatchlistItemOut nullable-on-failure precedent exactly (no deviation) -- a position is never dropped or the request 500'd just because its signal, specifically, couldn't be computed, even when its price/pnl are perfectly fine.
decisions.rationale: Rejected duplicating GET /api/portfolio/risk's own weekly-fetch-plus-caching logic into a shared helper in this change: get_risk's weekly fetch is entangled with its own protective_stop/evaluate_exit_flags pipeline and stops/weekly_by_id/daily_by_id caching, which has nothing to do with a fresh entry signal; forcing a shared abstraction now would couple two independently-evolving concerns (risk/exit evaluation vs. entry signal annotation) for a marginal reduction in one fetch call, especially since the underlying market data is already cached by app.data.cache regardless -- a second GET /api/portfolio/risk-style weekly fetch in the same request cycle is a cache hit in practice, not a real duplicate network round trip. Kept the new _compute_position_signal as a small, self-contained helper next to _ordered_positions instead, matching the narrow DataProviderError-only catch app.api.routers.watchlist._compute_signal already established (so a genuine bug in analyse() itself still surfaces as a loud 500 in tests/CI rather than being silently swallowed into a null field).

decisions.decision: Fixed the signal/price desync review comment on PR #118: _compute_position_signal now calls drop_malformed_daily_bars(e.daily_ohlcv) with its default require_full_ohlc_on_latest_bar=True (unchanged), but afterward checks whether the filtered frame's last row is still the same bar as e.daily_ohlcv's own last row (by index/date equality). If it isn't -- i.e. the latest bar failed the strict filter -- the function now returns None (nulling signal/confidence/confidence_band) instead of silently proceeding with the filtered frame (which would have computed the signal from the prior day's bar). Verified against app.portfolio.pricing._latest_close (only checks the latest bar's close for NaN, which is why e.daily_ohlcv is non-None at all whenever this desync can happen) and app.signals.engine.analyse (unlike evaluate_exit_flags, it genuinely reads the latest bar's open/high/low via Elder-Ray/Wave/Trigger, so get_risk's require_full_ohlc_on_latest_bar=False can't be safely reused here without feeding analyse() a bar it can't handle). Added TestGetPortfolioSignal.test_malformed_open_high_low_on_latest_bar_nulls_signal_but_not_price (backend/tests/integration/test_portfolio_get.py), mirroring test_portfolio_risk.py's analogous malformed-latest-bar fixture, asserting current_price stays populated from today's real close while signal/confidence/confidence_band go null instead of reflecting yesterday's bar.
decisions.rationale: Rejected passing require_full_ohlc_on_latest_bar=False through to analyse() (get_risk's fix, blind-copied): analyse() reads the latest bar's open/high/low directly (unlike evaluate_exit_flags, which only reads close), so a bar with NaN open/high/low would flow straight into indicator math and produce NaN/garbage Elder-Ray/Wave/Trigger results rather than degrading cleanly -- confirmed by reading app.signals.engine.analyse's own docstring and evaluate_wave/evaluate_trigger/evaluate_impulse's signatures, all of which take the full daily_ohlcv frame including open/high/low columns. Rejected silently computing the signal from the filtered (stale) frame as before: that's exactly the desync the review flagged -- no error, no null, just a one-day-stale signal next to a fresh price, which is worse than an explicit null because nothing in the response indicates it happened. Chose 'null the signal fields instead' over any richer alternative (e.g. exposing a separate 'signal_as_of' date) because it keeps PositionOut's existing nullable-on-failure contract exactly as documented (a position whose signal can't be computed right now gets null fields, full stop) rather than growing the schema for a narrow edge case -- also addressed the review's non-blocking finding (test asserting POST /api/portfolio/positions returns null signal/confidence/confidence_band) since it was a one-line addition to an existing test.

comments.summary: Blocking: `_compute_position_signal` (backend/app/api/routers/portfolio.py) filters `e.daily_ohlcv` with `drop_malformed_daily_bars`'s default `require_full_ohlc_on_latest_bar=True`, but `current_price`/`unrealized_pnl_pct` on the same position come from `app.portfolio.pricing._latest_close`, which only requires the latest bar's `close` to be non-NaN (permissive). When the latest daily bar has a valid `close` but NaN open/high/low -- the exact, already-observed yfinance condition `drop_malformed_daily_bars`'s own docstring documents, and the same condition `get_risk`'s docstring explicitly reasons about (citing the api-stocks-analysis-nullable-indicators-followups task) -- `current_price` reflects today's close while `signal`/`confidence`/`confidence_band` silently reflect yesterday's bar instead: no error, no null, just a one-day-stale signal displayed next to a fresh price. `get_risk` avoids this exact class of bug for its own fields by passing `require_full_ohlc_on_latest_bar=False`, but that's not a safe blind copy here either -- `analyse()` (unlike `evaluate_exit_flags`) does read the latest bar's open/high/low (Elder-Ray, Wave, Trigger), so `_compute_position_signal` needs its own reasoned fix for this desync, not either extreme unexamined. Neither this task's `decisions` entry nor `_compute_position_signal`'s docstring discusses this risk, and no test in `TestGetPortfolioSignal` exercises a malformed-latest-bar frame the way `test_portfolio_get.py`'s existing price-side malformed-bar fixtures do.

Non-blocking: no test asserts that `POST /api/portfolio/positions` (add_position) returns `signal`/`confidence`/`confidence_band` as null, even though the code explicitly sets them and API.md/openapi.json document it as intentional. `test_create_new_position_returns_201` (backend/tests/integration/test_portfolio_positions.py) only asserts `current_price`/`unrealized_pnl_pct` are null. Behavior is correct and documented, just untested explicitly -- filed as a follow-up.

review.notes: Checked out PR #118. Backend: 564 passed, 99.86% coverage (portfolio.py and schemas.py both 100%), matching the PR's claim. Frontend: vitest --coverage passed on a clean re-run (99.6% lines/branches; one PortfolioPage.test.tsx timeout on the first run reproduced as a flake under full-suite+coverage load, confirmed by isolating the test on both main and this branch where it passes in ~3.5s each time -- not a regression from this PR, which touches no frontend logic, only a regenerated types.ts). ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc all clean. `python scripts/export_openapi.py` re-run locally produces zero diff against the committed backend/openapi.json -- snapshot is current. No UI surface: grepped every portfolio-feature component/hook for `signal` and found none consuming the new fields yet, so the browser walkthrough and the e2e-test skill are correctly skipped (this PR is backend-only enrichment; frontend display is presumably a separate follow-on task). verify-elder-signal: `analyse()` itself is untouched and called with the same (ticker, daily_ohlcv, weekly_ohlcv) signature GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis and GET /api/watchlist already use -- no second/divergent signal computation, confirming the task's core requirement. architecture-review: router stays thin (the new helper only orchestrates fetch + null-handling, matching watchlist.py's existing `_compute_signal` precedent exactly), CachedDataProvider is used via the existing get_data_provider dependency (no re-fetch bypassing the SQLite cache), API.md/openapi.json/types.ts all updated consistently. The nullable-on-failure precedent, the weekly-fetch-per-position N+1 concern (mitigated by the existing 24h SQLite cache, consistent with get_risk's identical pattern), and add_position's null-on-write fields are all correctly implemented and documented per the task's `decisions` entry -- no issues there. The one blocking finding above (a latent-but-real signal/price staleness desync on a documented yfinance data condition, unaddressed by the decisions entry and untested) is why this is needs_work rather than accepted with a follow-up; it's about signal correctness, not a nit. Ran the code-review skill (medium effort, backgrounded) against the diff; it independently surfaced the same desync finding as its one reported result, which I verified directly against `_latest_close`'s close-only NaN check before including it.
